To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
P. stipitis can produce high ethanol concentrations, even in the presence of inhibitors, and the acetic acid concentration is a critical factor in ethanol production.
the presence of acetic acid, in the concentrations studied, has a significant negative effect on ethanol production by the yeast P. stipitis, while furfural and HMF do not show significant effect.
the ethanol yield and productivity of P. stipitis were significantly affected by acetic acid, while furfural and HMF had no effect on the ethanol production.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a model for ethanol production by P. stipitis in a mixture of inhibitors, based on the response surface methodology, with the aim of predicting the ethanol production in a complex culture medium, with the presence of the major inhibitors of lignin pretreatments.

the effect of inhibitors in the production of ethanol by P. stipitis, and it is concluded that this microorganism can be used in the production of bioethanol, but with the presence of inhibitors at low levels.

the development of an efficient fermentation process for ethanol production, using lignocellulosics biomass, and with the identification of the optimal conditions of fermentation in a complex culture medium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best results for ethanol production by P. stipitis were obtained in the absence of inhibitors.
P. stipitis can produce ethanol in the presence of acetic acid, HMF and furfural.
the presence of inhibitors in lignocellulosics biomass pretreatment is an obstacle to the development of ethanol production processes from biomass.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

P. stipitis can ferment xylose to ethanol in the presence of inhibitors, with a maximum ethanol concentration of 2.4 g L -1 and 1.5 g L -1 of xylose consumption in a complex culture medium, at 0.75 and 2.25 g L -1, respectively, of acetic acid, and no influence of furfurals.
acetic acid has the most significant influence on ethanol production, and that the presence of inhibitors in the culture media does not affect the ethanol yield.
the presence of acetic acid and HMF in the culture media, at the concentrations tested, did not affect significantly ethanol production by P. stipitis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of P. stipitis in the presence of inhibitors is possible, with the use of a mixture of inhibitors at low concentrations, and that the use of a complex culture media is essential for the production of ethanol.
the presence of acetic acid in the fermentation media, in addition to furfural and HMF, is the major factor that affects the production of ethanol by P. Stipitis.
the use of P. stipitis in a culture media containing xylose and a mixture of the major inhibitors of pretreatment of lignocellulose, is feasible.
